# MM-P3-L4-HT02-S2 Fastener inspection and torque - Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2

Revision: Rev E  
Plant: P3, line P3-L4  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L4-HT02

Scope
- This document defines the required fastener inspection, cleaning, lubrication, and torque verification activities for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2, EQ-P3-L4-HT02, during scheduled preventive maintenance and after component replacement or repair. It supplements general procedures in MM-P3-L4-HT02 and operational controls in SOP-P3-L4-01 and provides specific fastener handling guidance referenced in SB-1043.

Background and rationale
- Fasteners on EQ-P3-L4-HT02 are subject to repeated thermal cycling and exposure to quench media. Proper inspection, cleaning, and lubrication prevent galling, maintain clamp load, and reduce risk of loosening that can lead to part damage or process variation. Lubricant selection and quench timing are critical contextual controls for this equipment. The quench delay maximum for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P3-L4-HT02) is 20 seconds. This constraint affects how fastener servicing interfaces with furnace cycles and quench operations.
- Use of the specified lubricant maintains repeatable friction conditions at the mating surfaces of non-sealed fasteners and ensures more consistent applied torque translates to target clamp load. The lubricant part number for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P3-L4-HT02) is CFW-LUB-407.

Tools
- Hand torque tool calibrated per facility calibration program; follow calibration records and acceptance per MM-P3-L4-HT02.
- Clean, lint‑free rags and approved cleaning solvent per SOP-P3-L4-01.
- Soft nylon brush for thread cleaning to preserve plating.
- Inspection mirror and bright task light for visual assessment of flank contact and seat surfaces.
- Fastener boards or trays to control orientation and prevent loss of hardware.
- Personal protective equipment as required in SOP-P3-L4-01.

Procedure
- Preparation
  - Review MM-P3-L4-HT02 and SB-1043 for any component-specific fastener requirements before starting work.
  - Coordinate with operations to confirm furnace is in a maintenance state and that quench operations will not begin while fasteners are being handled, respecting the quench delay maximum for EQ-P3-L4-HT02. Allow operations to acknowledge that quench initiation will be deferred to avoid quench‑related thermal shock during mechanical servicing.
  - Lay out tools and parts in designated clean area. Verify torque tool calibration status against the current calibration record.

- Fastener removal and inspection
  - Remove fasteners carefully, controlling orientation and storing hardware in trays to prevent contamination.
  - Visually inspect threads, bearing surface, and head for wear, corrosion, galling, strip, or any deformation that could affect clamping performance. Use inspection mirror and light for concealed surfaces.
  - Clean fasteners with approved solvent and nylon brush. Dry immediately and inspect again.
  - Reject any fastener exhibiting compromised thread form, significant corrosion, or damage. Refer to MM-P3-L4-HT02 for disposition and replacement guidance.

- Preparation prior to reassembly
  - Clean mating threads and bearing surfaces on equipment. Remove old lubricant, carbon, scale, and foreign material per SOP-P3-L4-01.
  - Apply lubricant CFW-LUB-407 to mating threads and to the underside of bolt heads or nut faces where required. Apply uniformly to the threaded portion that will be engaged, wiping away excess so that only a light, even film remains. Document lot or batch identification of lubricant used on the maintenance record.

- Torque application and verification
  - Assemble fasteners hand tight to ensure proper alignment and seating. Use the torque tool to apply torque in a controlled sequence that ensures even loading of the assembly; follow the sequence recommended in MM-P3-L4-HT02 for the specific component, or use a star or cross pattern where no specific sequence is provided.
  - Apply torque using the calibrated torque tool. Do not substitute a non-calibrated tool. If a documented clamp load target is required, refer to MM-P3-L4-HT02 for required values; otherwise follow the assembly guidance in MM-P3-L4-HT02 and SOP-P3-L4-01.
  - After initial torque application, allow a short settle period per maintenance practice then recheck torque to confirm retention. If torque values vary beyond acceptable repeatability as defined in MM-P3-L4-HT02, investigate for relaxation causes such as embedment, cross‑threading, or incorrect lubricant application.

Acceptance criteria
- Fasteners are accepted for service when:
  - Threads and bearing surfaces show no evidence of damage that would prevent proper clamp load transfer as defined by inspection criteria in MM-P3-L4-HT02.
  - Lubricant applied is CFW-LUB-407 and lot identification is recorded.
  - Torque application was performed with a calibrated tool and the post‑assembly verification shows retention within the repeatability limits defined in MM-P3-L4-HT02.
  - Operating controls respecting the quench delay maximum for EQ-P3-L4-HT02 were confirmed with operations prior to returning equipment to service.

Examples and clarifications
- Example: During inspection of a vacuum jacket cover, threads that show light surface corrosion that can be fully cleaned without loss of thread form may be reused after cleaning and lubricant application. Threads with crest damage or galling that reduces clearance require replacement per MM-P3-L4-HT02.
- Clarification: Application of CFW-LUB-407 is required only to the surfaces specified in component documentation and MM-P3-L4-HT02; do not apply to threadlocker surfaces unless explicitly directed in SB-1043 or MM-P3-L4-HT02.

Records to keep
- Maintenance log entry that includes equipment id EQ-P3-L4-HT02, description of work, name of technician, date, and time.
- Torque verification strip or printout from calibrated torque tool for the job, filed with maintenance records.
- Lubricant usage record including lubricant part number CFW-LUB-407 and lot identification.
- Disposition records for any replaced fasteners, referenced to MM-P3-L4-HT02 and SB-1043 where applicable.
- A note in the work order attesting that operations were notified and that the quench delay maximum for EQ-P3-L4-HT02 was observed during the task.

References
- MM-P3-L4-HT02
- SB-1043
- SOP-P3-L4-01

End of document.
